**Verdict**
Quality score: **6/10**. The code is small, readable, and covered by a passing pytest suite, but I would **not approve as-is** because there are real data correctness issues around ingestion atomicity and timestamp handling.

Tests run: `python -m pytest -q` passed, 12 tests. `compileall` could not complete because this workspace is read-only for `__pycache__` creation.

**Issues**
- [src/jobwatch/cli.py](/work/src/jobwatch/cli.py:83): **high** - Failed ingests still persist valid rows before the malformed-row threshold check rejects the file.
- [src/jobwatch/parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:109): **high** - Timestamps are validated but stored unnormalized, so date-only, space-separated, and offset-aware inputs can compare incorrectly later.
- [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:114): **high** - Report queries compare timestamp strings lexicographically instead of using a canonical datetime representation.
- [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:177): **medium** - `MAX(COALESCE(...))` and trailing-window logic inherit the same text-order timestamp bug.
- [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:18): **medium** - Read-only report commands call `connect()`, which silently creates and initializes a new empty database on a mistyped path.
- [src/jobwatch/store.py](/work/src/jobwatch/store.py:11): **medium** - Failure reports only include `FAILED`, `TIMEOUT`, and `OOM`, excluding other Slurm terminal/non-success states such as `CANCELLED`, `NODE_FAIL`, `BOOT_FAIL`, `DEADLINE`, and `PREEMPTED`; Slurm also documents `OUT_OF_MEMORY` as the long state name for OOM. ([slurm.schedmd.com](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacct.html?utm_source=openai))
- [src/jobwatch/parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:91): **medium** - GPU TRES parsing is too loose: it accepts negative counts, matches any key starting with `gres/gpu`, and can silently undercount malformed/composite values.
- [src/jobwatch/cli.py](/work/src/jobwatch/cli.py:20): **low** - Custom argparse error handling raises `SystemExit` with a string, producing exit status 1 instead of the conventional parser error status 2.
- [src/jobwatch/parsing.py](/work/src/jobwatch/parsing.py:175): **low** - `parse_file()` materializes all records and emits one warning per bad row, which will scale poorly on large accounting exports.
- [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:13): **low** - Project config has tests only; there is no linting, formatting, type checking, or CI-visible quality gate configured.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **170 lines**. That includes production fixes plus focused tests for atomic ingest, timestamp normalization/range queries, failure-state coverage, DB-open behavior, and GPU parsing.

issues.description: Failed ingests still persist valid rows before the malformed-row threshold check rejects the file.
Timestamps are validated but stored unnormalized, causing downstream date range comparisons to be incorrect for accepted ISO variants.
Report queries compare timestamp text lexicographically instead of comparing canonical datetimes.
Newest-record and trailing-window calculations depend on text ordering of timestamps.
Report commands silently create a new empty database when the requested DB path is missing.
Failure reports exclude several terminal non-success Slurm states and only recognize a narrow hard-coded set.
GPU TRES parsing accepts negative counts and can undercount or overmatch malformed GPU keys.
Argparse errors exit with status 1 instead of the conventional parser-error status 2.
File parsing loads every valid record into memory and can spam one warning per malformed row on large exports.
Project lacks linting, formatting, type checking, or CI quality gate configuration.
